title: Buying a Business Just for the Job? Yes, Please.

 Buying a Business Just for the Job? Yes, Please.
Sara,
Some folks buy businesses the way you’d buy an investment property: polish it up, raise the rates, flip it for more.
Others? They’re just looking for a really, really good job. And guess what? That’s not only okay—it’s smart.
I see two big groups who should absolutely buy a business with the goal of running it themselves:
1. The Relocators

Moving to small-town America? Trading your city commute for a lake view, golf course, or fly-fishing stream? The problem is, high-paying jobs don’t grow on trees in those zip codes.
But you know what does exist? That local Main Street accounting firm whose owner is ready to retire. Buy it, and you’re not just getting income; you’re buying your instantaneous ticket into the fabric of the community. That’s priceless.
2. The “Not-So-Newbies” 

If you’re 22 with no mortgage and zero dependents, sure, bootstrapping a firm from scratch might work. But if you’ve already built a life (and taken on a mortgage) based on making $150K a year, slow growth isn’t cute.
Buying a firm with an SBA loan means you can step straight into a business that already covers your lifestyle and gives you a platform to grow from. Instead of slogging through 10 years of “grind,” you start with something that feels like year 11.
The takeaway? Buying a business isn’t always about “the exit.” Sometimes it’s about building a life you actually want to live—today.
